findings.summary: The admission rule only checks plans that declare mirrored_sources, so a plan that mirrors a source and declares nothing gets past admission
findings.evidence: An empty list gives no finding, so catching the omission the request names ('a plan that leaves this out') depends only on the prose rule in the critic prompt. The CHANGELOG and the design doc both say this ('Left out: a keyword trigger…'; 'does not close failure class f62n by itself'), which fits the mechanism default. Still, the mechanism does not cover the f62n case where the planner never notices it is mirroring a source.

summary: The candidate fails because the test runs could not be confirmed, not because of any fault I found in the content. The planner and critic prompts state the convention as asked. The CHANGELOG entry cites f62n and the four introspections. A shape check for the new optional `mirrored_sources` plan section (an admission rule) is added. The new tests at the unit, refusal-corpus and full-job level each pair a fixture that lists no places (rejected) with the same fixture listing them (accepted). But Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` for this commit failed in CI on an unrelated-looking drain test, `drain::tests::status_and_stop_find_the_drain_by_pid_file_when_command_lines_contain_drain`, and the test shard did not finish. I could not rerun it or the new tests: this snapshot fails to compile against stale athena-data artifacts in the shared build directory, apparently left by Athena's scratch build with the fix reverted, and policy denied a fresh `--target-dir`. As a result, criteria 3, 5 and 6 are unshown. To pass, rerun the tests on a clean build directory. If the drain test turns out to be flaky and the `mirror` and `budget` tests pass, I see no blocker in the content.
